name: Itchy Scalp
description: An itchy scalp is a common condition that can be caused by various factors such as dermatitis, dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, or other underlying health issues.
symptoms: Scaly or flaky skin on the scalp
Possible hair loss in severe cases
recommended_ingredients: Corticosteroids (for severe cases under medical supervision)
ingredients_to_avoid: Sulfates (as they can irritate the scalp)
recommended_product_categories: Scalp treatments containing active ingredients like salicylic acid or coal tar

daily_routine.purpose: To cleanse the scalp without causing irritation
To address and prevent flakiness and itching

professional_treatments: In-office scalp treatments (e.g., light therapy for psoriasis)
natural_remedies: Applying a mixture of coconut oil and tea tree oil to the scalp
Using apple cider vinegar as a rinse after shampooing
lifestyle_tips: Regularly wash your pillowcases and hats
Limit the use of heat styling tools on your hair
Avoid scratching the scalp, which can worsen irritation
common_myths: Itchy scalp is always due to dandruff
Using hot water for washing hair will make it cleaner.
when_to_consult_doctor: If symptoms persist despite home remedies or if there is significant hair loss, redness, or signs of infection.
prevention: Maintain a balanced diet and good hygiene habits
Avoid harsh chemicals in hair care products

severity_levels.mild: Mild itching with occasional flakiness. Can be managed with over-the-counter treatments.
severity_levels.moderate: Frequent itching, more noticeable flakiness or redness. May require prescription treatments for effective management.
severity_levels.severe: Intense itching and visible signs of inflammation, possibly leading to significant hair loss. Requires immediate medical attention.

expert_tips: Regularly check your scalp for changes in color, texture, or presence of lice
Stay informed about new treatments and products that can help manage itchy scalp
